transcript.text: and0 on the duel against Ian. So guys,
in the second game here against Ian, I
decided to go for Lava Hound because I
did feel like Lava Hound would be pretty
like unpredictable for me. I hadn't used
a single Lava Hound deck in all of CRL
this month. So I just thought that it
would be a very very good idea to just
remain unpredictable because I didn't
think that he would end up countering
it. And guys, I'm not sure if you
noticed what just happened there, but he
dropped a berserker at the bridge and he
dropped skeletons. And I don't know if
you guys um remember what I said in the
beginning of the video, but it is a dual
format and you were unable to repeat
cards. So guys, that meant right there
that Ian not only repeated Berserker,
but he also repeated skeleton. So no
matter what happened in this game as a
result, I was guaranteed to win the
game. Guys, honestly, at this point, I
was so happy because I knew that the
odds of me qualifying after that were
extremely extremely high, but I knew
that like I still wanted to win the game
because even though like I had the game
one, I do need crowns for tiebreers. And
that's really important. Um like there
is a lot of different tiebreers, but the
two main tiebreers are number one game
difference. So, your win to loss
difference. So, you still want to win
the game. And the second um tiebreaker
is the crown difference. So if you have
a completely tied match history and um
and all of that stuff, then it it goes
to the crowns. So I actually played this
out wanting to get two to three crowns
if possible. So that's like the reason I
was actually still like playing this.
Otherwise, I would have probably just
given up, right? Cuz you know, I won the
game already because of his repeat. It
was actually important for that because
in the third month, two months ago,
guys, I actually qualified because I got
one more crown than my um other
competitor and I actually qualified off
of that. It was actually crazy. Like we
had the exact same win rate, same game
difference, everything. The only thing
that was different was the crowns. So,
ever since then, I've always made it a
very big um thing for me to try to get
as many crowns as possible, even in an
already won game. So, here I went for
the skelly drags on the bomber and then
I went for the inferno dragon as well. I
wasn't trying like crazy hard to defend
this because I wanted to get the three
crown cuz I knew that Ian's deck had no
air defense which was very like lucky by
me. I feel like even if he didn't like
repeat it wouldn't have mattered. He
actually did text me. He's like, "Dude,
I didn't even realize I repeated a card,
I was so locked in." And I thought that
was kind of funny. Um and it even makes
sense as well because of course you're
never going to repeat a card on purpose
or anything like that cuz then you just
like completely lose out. Here I went
for a rune giant in the pocket just to
boost up all my cards again. And then I
went for another inferno dragon. I knew
that if he really wanted to, he would be
able to keep on defending. But the thing
is, right, I just assumed that he would
give up. But I think at the same time,
he didn't end up giving up because he
wanted to also like not give me crowns.
I think that was the whole point of him
playing off is that like I don't think
that he actually thought he was going to
win from this position. I just think
that he really thought that like um like
if he gives me the three crowns or
something then it it it could actually
like hurt him in the future or something
like that. So here I just made sure to
keep defending and I went for the skelly
drags on defense as well just making
sure to take this all out and to be
honest he was playing well but I do feel
like that I wasn't playing my 100%
knowing that I was already winning the
game no matter what because of the uh
repeat here. I went for the inferno
dragon on the king tower because like I
said I did really want the three crown
if possible. He was making it really
hard to get it. And I think it was
around after this defense, like right
here after he snowballed, I was like,
"Okay, like I'm just never going to get
the three crown." Like, I just kind of
accepted it that he was not going to let
me get the three crown. And if I kept
going for it, there was a chance that I
could lose cuz in this uh lava deck,
even though lava does counter drill, no
air defense really hard, I don't
actually have any drill defense. Like I
don't have a Valkyrie or anything like
that. So, there was a real possibility
that I could choke the game if I wasn't
careful. So, I just decided like, screw
this, bro. I'm just going to win the
game normally because if if I keep going
for this, then I could actually lose.
So, here I went for the berserker here,
just making sure to take out his
berserker. I went for the inferno dragon
at the bridge as well, kind of just
knowing that, you know, this game was
over. I went for a rune giant here, and
I just started fireball cycling in a
second. I just made sure to cage on
defense once again because I knew that I
only needed like two more fireballs and
two zaps to finish off the game. I did
zap first just to help get to the EVO. I
firedalled that berserker just trying to
get some lava puff spits on the tower.
And right now we were a fireball zap
away from winning the game. So I went
for another cage here, guys. I went for
the skeleton dragons. He did switch it
up with the lava I mean with the drill
in the back, but it didn't really
matter. I went for the fireball here,
and that was a good game, guys. And I
beat Ian two to zero to bring me to a
really good spot to qualify for the
world finals.
